[F002] Both findings are fixed and verified.

**Finding 1 (high/correctness — locked proof obligations can be erased before close):** `evaluate_close_proofs` no longer derives obligations solely from the mutable live contract. New `read_score_sidecar()` / `close_obligations()` in `outcome_score.py:747-900` read the lock-time sidecar and treat every recorded slice as an obligation whose method, `proof_refs` and label come from the *lock-time* record — so deleting a slice, deleting the whole `objective_contract.json`, or swapping its `proof.method` after the lock no longer retires the proof. `_drift_note()` names how the contract moved (`slice … no longer in the contract`, `proof method changed after lock (walk → named_test)`, changed capability/proof_refs) inside the close refusal, and points at the documented escape (a `proof_gap_deferred` entry), not a contract edit. Slices added after the lock remain obligations from the live score, and a plan with no sidecar (anything locked before this artifact existed) keeps the previous live-contract behaviour exactly. Six regression tests cover lock → edit-contract → close for delete-slice, delete-contract, method swap, paid-anyway, still-deferrable, added-after-lock, and the no-sidecar fallback.

**Finding 2 (high/correctness — `delivers: [{}]` bypasses the missing-outcome refusal):** new public `slice_defects()` (`outcome_score.py:352-386`) mirrors `objective_contract.schema.json`'s four `required` fields plus its 10-character `capability`
